newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe's industrial index ends Monday weaker.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe's industrial index ends Monday weaker.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial index closed weaker on Monday, on the back of continued investor uncertainty over government's annual budget as well as recent poor results in some counters.
"The market continues its current sideways movement due to prebudget uncertainty," one broker said.
"Finhold's interims came out today showing heavy interest payments reducing...attributable profits," the broker added.
Sugar grower Hippo Valley Estates also had a poor showing for the previous financial year.

Brokers expect the lull in the bourse to continue as long as attractive rates on the local money market continue luring away investors. They say the market can only find direction from the government's budget announcement towards the end of July.

Counters to trade weaker on Monday included Finhold which tumbled 150 cents to 400 while blue chip bankers Barclays eased 30 cents to 3,200 and pork producers Colcom were down 45 cents at 410. Bankers NMB put off 50 cents to 3,100. The key industrial index shed 20.71 points to close at 10,275.39.
Minings traded largely unchanged but the seven-share index there managed to inch up 0.09 points to 958.19.
